questions.question_text: What is Object-Oriented Programming (OOP)?

answer_key.model_answer: Object-Oriented Programming is a programming approach in which a program is organized around classes and objects rather than only functions and procedures. An object represents a real-world entity and contains data (attributes) and functions (methods) that operate on that data.
answer_key.marking_rubric: 1 mark for the programming approach; 1 mark for classes and objects; 1 mark for data and methods.
answer_key.important_keywords: Object-Oriented Programming, classes, objects, attributes, methods

questions.question_text: What is a class in C++?

answer_key.model_answer: A class is a blueprint or template for creating objects. It defines the data and functions that an object can have. For example, Student can be a class containing rollNo, name and display().
answer_key.marking_rubric: 1 mark for blueprint/template; 1 mark for defining data and functions; 1 mark for a suitable example.
answer_key.important_keywords: class, blueprint, template, data members, member functions

questions.question_text: What is an object? Give an example.

answer_key.model_answer: An object is an instance of a class. It represents a real-world entity and can access the members of its class. For example, if Student is a class, student1 is an object of that class.
answer_key.marking_rubric: 1 mark for instance of class; 1 mark for representing an entity; 1 mark for example.
answer_key.important_keywords: object, instance, class, student1

questions.question_text: Define encapsulation.

answer_key.model_answer: Encapsulation means combining data and the functions that operate on that data into a single unit, usually a class. It also helps control access to data using access specifiers such as private, public and protected.
answer_key.marking_rubric: 1 mark for combining data and functions; 1 mark for single unit/class; 1 mark for access control.
answer_key.important_keywords: encapsulation, data, functions, class, access specifiers

questions.question_text: What is abstraction? Give one example.

answer_key.model_answer: Abstraction means showing only the necessary details to the user while hiding unnecessary implementation details. For example, we use an ATM without knowing the internal implementation of the banking system.
answer_key.marking_rubric: 1 mark for showing necessary details; 1 mark for hiding implementation details; 1 mark for example.
answer_key.important_keywords: abstraction, essential details, implementation details, ATM

questions.question_text: Define inheritance and state one advantage.

answer_key.model_answer: Inheritance allows one class to acquire properties and methods of another class. It promotes code reuse. For example, Car can inherit common properties and methods from Vehicle.
answer_key.marking_rubric: 1 mark for definition; 1 mark for acquiring properties/methods; 1 mark for advantage or example.
answer_key.important_keywords: inheritance, base class, derived class, properties, code reuse

questions.question_text: What is polymorphism? Give two examples.

answer_key.model_answer: Polymorphism means one interface or name can have multiple forms or behaviours. Examples include function overloading and method overriding.
answer_key.marking_rubric: 1 mark for meaning; 1 mark for first example; 1 mark for second example.
answer_key.important_keywords: polymorphism, multiple forms, function overloading, method overriding

questions.question_text: What is data hiding in OOP?

answer_key.model_answer: Data hiding restricts direct access to the internal data of an object. Access specifiers such as private, protected and public are used to control access to class members.
answer_key.marking_rubric: 1 mark for restricting direct access; 1 mark for internal data; 1 mark for access specifiers.
answer_key.important_keywords: data hiding, private, protected, public, access control

questions.question_text: What is message passing in OOP?

answer_key.model_answer: Message passing is the way objects communicate with each other. Objects communicate by calling methods and passing information or arguments.
answer_key.marking_rubric: 1 mark for object communication; 1 mark for calling methods; 1 mark for passing information.
answer_key.important_keywords: message passing, objects, methods, arguments, communication

questions.question_text: Write any three differences between POP and OOP.

answer_key.model_answer: 1. POP divides a program into functions, while OOP divides it into classes and objects. 2. POP mainly focuses on functions, while OOP focuses on objects and data. 3. POP generally follows a top-down approach, while OOP generally follows a bottom-up approach.
answer_key.marking_rubric: 1 mark for each correct difference.
answer_key.important_keywords: POP, OOP, functions, classes, objects, top-down, bottom-up

questions.question_text: What is a data type in C++?

answer_key.model_answer: A data type specifies the type of data that a variable can store. It also determines the memory required and the operations that can be performed on the data.
answer_key.marking_rubric: 1 mark for type of data; 1 mark for variable storage; 1 mark for memory or operations.
answer_key.important_keywords: data type, variable, memory, operations

questions.question_text: Name the four broad categories of C++ data types.

answer_key.model_answer: The four broad categories are: 1. Basic or fundamental data types. 2. Derived data types. 3. User-defined data types. 4. Void data type.
answer_key.marking_rubric: Award 0.75 mark for each correct category.
answer_key.important_keywords: basic, derived, user-defined, void

questions.question_text: Give any three examples of basic data types with their uses.

answer_key.model_answer: 1. int – stores integer numbers. 2. char – stores a single character. 3. float – stores decimal numbers. Other basic types include double and bool.
answer_key.marking_rubric: 1 mark for each correct type and use.
answer_key.important_keywords: int, char, float, integer, character, decimal

questions.question_text: What are derived data types? Give three examples.

answer_key.model_answer: Derived data types are created from fundamental data types. Examples include array, pointer, function and reference.
answer_key.marking_rubric: 1 mark for definition; 2 marks for any three correct examples.
answer_key.important_keywords: derived data types, fundamental types, array, pointer, function, reference

questions.question_text: What are user-defined data types? Give three examples.

answer_key.model_answer: User-defined data types are created by the programmer. Examples include class, struct, union and enum.
answer_key.marking_rubric: 1 mark for definition; 2 marks for any three examples.
answer_key.important_keywords: user-defined, programmer, class, struct, union, enum

questions.question_text: What are keywords in C++? Give any four examples.

answer_key.model_answer: Keywords are reserved words in C++ that have a predefined meaning to the compiler. They cannot normally be used as names of variables, functions or classes. Examples are int, if, class and return.
answer_key.marking_rubric: 1 mark for reserved words; 1 mark for predefined meaning/restriction; 1 mark for examples.
answer_key.important_keywords: keywords, reserved words, compiler, int, if, class, return

questions.question_text: What is a variable? Give an example.

answer_key.model_answer: A variable is a named memory location used to store data. Its value can change during program execution. Example: int age = 20; Here, age is a variable of type int.
answer_key.marking_rubric: 1 mark for named memory location; 1 mark for storing/changeable data; 1 mark for example.
answer_key.important_keywords: variable, named memory location, data, int age

questions.question_text: What is variable declaration? Write its syntax and one example.

answer_key.model_answer: Variable declaration tells the compiler the name and data type of a variable. Syntax: data_type variable_name; Example: int age;
answer_key.marking_rubric: 1 mark for meaning; 1 mark for syntax; 1 mark for example.
answer_key.important_keywords: variable declaration, data type, variable name, int age

questions.question_text: What is variable initialization? Give one example.

answer_key.model_answer: Initialization means assigning an initial value to a variable at the time of declaration. Example: int age = 20; Here, age is declared and initialized with the value 20.
answer_key.marking_rubric: 1 mark for meaning; 1 mark for assigning initial value at declaration; 1 mark for example.
answer_key.important_keywords: initialization, initial value, declaration, int age = 20

questions.question_text: What is dynamic initialization of a variable?

answer_key.model_answer: Dynamic initialization means initializing a variable with a value that is determined at run time rather than being fixed directly in the source code. Example: int sum = a + b;
answer_key.marking_rubric: 1 mark for initialization; 1 mark for run-time value; 1 mark for example.
answer_key.important_keywords: dynamic initialization, run time, calculated value, int sum

questions.question_text: What is a reference variable? Give its syntax.

answer_key.model_answer: A reference variable is an alternative name or alias for an existing variable. It is declared using the & symbol. Syntax: data_type &reference_name = variable_name;
answer_key.marking_rubric: 1 mark for alias meaning; 1 mark for & symbol; 1 mark for correct syntax.
answer_key.important_keywords: reference variable, alias, ampersand (&), existing variable

questions.question_text: What happens when a reference variable is modified?

answer_key.model_answer: A reference variable is another name for an existing variable. Therefore, changing the reference also changes the original variable. For example, if ref refers to a, assigning ref = 20 changes a to 20.
answer_key.marking_rubric: 1 mark for alias relationship; 1 mark for effect on original variable; 1 mark for example/explanation.
answer_key.important_keywords: reference, alias, original variable, value changes

questions.question_text: What is Dynamic Memory Allocation (DMA)?

answer_key.model_answer: Dynamic Memory Allocation is the process of allocating and releasing memory during program execution. In C++, memory can be allocated using new and released using delete.
answer_key.marking_rubric: 1 mark for allocating memory; 1 mark for run-time allocation/release; 1 mark for new and delete.
answer_key.important_keywords: DMA, memory allocation, run time, new, delete

questions.question_text: What is the use of the new and delete operators in C++?

answer_key.model_answer: The new operator allocates memory dynamically during program execution. The delete operator releases memory that was allocated using new. They help manage dynamically allocated memory.
answer_key.marking_rubric: 1 mark for new; 1 mark for delete; 1 mark for purpose.
answer_key.important_keywords: new, delete, allocate, release, dynamic memory

questions.question_text: Differentiate between new and new[] operators.

answer_key.model_answer: The new operator is used to allocate memory for a single object. The new[] operator is used to allocate memory for an array of objects or elements.
answer_key.marking_rubric: 1.5 marks for each correct use.
answer_key.important_keywords: new, new[], single object, array allocation

questions.question_text: What is the scope resolution operator in C++?

answer_key.model_answer: The scope resolution operator is represented by ::. It is used to specify the scope to which a name belongs. It can be used to access a global variable, define a member function outside a class, or access namespace members.
answer_key.marking_rubric: 1 mark for :: symbol; 1 mark for specifying scope; 1 mark for any correct use.
answer_key.important_keywords: scope resolution, ::, global variable, member function, namespace

questions.question_text: What are manipulators in C++? Give any two examples.

answer_key.model_answer: Manipulators are used with input and output streams to control the formatting of data. Examples include endl, which moves output to the next line, and setw(), which sets the minimum width of the next output field.
answer_key.marking_rubric: 1 mark for purpose; 1 mark for first example/use; 1 mark for second example/use.
answer_key.important_keywords: manipulators, stream, formatting, endl, setw

questions.question_text: What is the use of setprecision() and setfill() manipulators?

answer_key.model_answer: setprecision() controls the precision of floating-point output. setfill() specifies the character used to fill unused field width, usually with setw(). Both are available through the iomanip header.
answer_key.marking_rubric: 1 mark for setprecision; 1 mark for setfill; 1 mark for iomanip or correct explanation.
answer_key.important_keywords: setprecision(), setfill(), floating-point, field width, iomanip

questions.question_text: What is a function call? Write its general syntax.

answer_key.model_answer: A function call is a statement or expression used to execute a function. Control is transferred to the function, its statements are executed, and control returns to the calling point. Syntax: function_name(arguments);
answer_key.marking_rubric: 1 mark for executing a function; 1 mark for control transfer and return; 1 mark for syntax.
answer_key.important_keywords: function call, execute, control transfer, arguments, syntax

questions.question_text: What is a default argument in C++? Give an example.

answer_key.model_answer: A default argument is a value assigned to a function parameter in advance. If the function call does not provide a value for that parameter, the default value is used. Example: void display(int x = 10);
answer_key.marking_rubric: 1 mark for definition; 1 mark for when it is used; 1 mark for example.
answer_key.important_keywords: default argument, parameter, default value, function call
